description: Create the service layer foundation in src/services/ - async StorageService, HotkeyService, and SessionService that run in the main process (CommonJS). These provide cleaner abstractions over the raw storage.js and window.js code.
steps: Create src/services/StorageService.js - CommonJS module. Class with: constructor() initializes in-memory caches for config/preferences/keybinds/windowState/credentials. async init() loads all data from storage.js into cache. getPreferences()/getConfig()/etc return cached data (sync). updatePreference(key, value) updates cache immediately, schedules debounced flush (200ms) to storage.js writeJsonFile. Same pattern for updateConfig, updateWindowState, etc. Exposes same operations as storage.js but cached + async flush. Uses existing storage.js functions internally (require('../storage')).

Create src/services/HotkeyService.js - CommonJS module. Class with: constructor(globalShortcut). register(accelerator, callback) - registers and tracks. unregister(accelerator) - unregisters single binding. updateBindings(newKeybinds, handlers) - diffs against current registered set, only changes what changed (not full rebuild). getRegistered() - returns currently registered bindings. Uses Electron globalShortcut internally.

Create src/services/SessionService.js - CommonJS module. Class extends EventEmitter. Owns geminiSessionRef. Methods: start(params), stop(), isActive(), getStatus(), getSessionId(). Emits 'started', 'stopped', 'error', 'reconnecting'. Tracks reconnection state. Route-independent - lives as singleton in main process.
Create src/services/index.js - CommonJS barrel export of all services.
acceptance_criteria: src/services/StorageService.js exports a class that caches storage reads and debounces writes
src/services/HotkeyService.js exports a class that supports incremental hotkey registration
src/services/SessionService.js exports a class that manages session lifecycle independently of UI
All service files use CommonJS (require/module.exports) since they run in main process
Services use existing storage.js and Electron APIs internally
verification: Run: node -e "require('./src/services')" to confirm all services load without error
